scientific_question: Can a mechanism-aligned state-conditioned adaptation of already-retrieved memory produce a modest prospective first-action uptake increase after a simple explicit-use reminder failed?

interpretation.supported: State-conditioned binding produces a higher aggregate branch-specific first-action uptake than native reuse and a memory-only adapter on this fresh pilot, showing that a mechanism-aligned transformation can reopen the diagnosed exposure-to-uptake path in some states.
interpretation.not_supported: A broadly consistent or universal repair. The effect is sparse and sign-heterogeneous and does not pass the frozen cross-state consistency gate.
interpretation.why_useful_for_paper: The engineering section now has a bounded proof of concept: a simple salience reminder fails, whereas state-conditioned adaptation has a nonzero aggregate transport opening. The main novelty remains problem formulation, stage-resolved diagnosis, and diagnostic completeness rather than method performance.
interpretation.novelty_boundary: State-aware memory is already published work (e.g. SAMem, Findings ACL 2026); this adapter is intentionally used as a diagnostic validation probe and is not claimed as a new memory architecture.

quality_boundaries.binder_format_noncompliance: One A2 binder output (task 47 success branch) exceeds the requested 60-word format; that state has zero uptake in all arms and does not drive the positive aggregate cells.
quality_boundaries.posthoc_note_divergence_status: hypothesis generation only; not used to reopen the untouched holdout

paper_revision.claim_style: heterogeneous proof-of-concept opening; not general repair pass

reopen_condition: Do not tune SCMB prompts or an applicability threshold on the 12 pilot states and then consume the 19-state holdout. A future confirmatory test requires a separately frozen applicability rule justified independently of policy outcomes and explicit new authority.
